title: Same $200 a Month, 10 Years Apart: $281,000 Gap

scenes.say: Mia and Luis both invest $200 a month. At 65, they're about $281,000 apart.
The only difference? Mia started at 25. Luis started at 35.
Mia puts in about $96,000 total. Luis puts in $72,000.
Say it earns roughly 7% a year in an index fund. Not guaranteed, just an example.
Mia's money grows slowly, then much faster in the last decades.
At 65, Mia has about $525,000. Luis has about $244,000.
Only $24,000 more from Mia. Most of the gap is time doing the work.
When did you start? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because it's the same $200, and $281,000 apart.
